trigger: reveal a Persian line of text
code: const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0,0.45)); ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(0,y-h, W, h*1.6); ctx.clip(); ctx.fillText(line, x, y + (1-p)*h*0.55); ctx.restore();
do: Mask is the full Persian line box (>=1.5em) so dots above and the yeh tail below are never cut; per line add i*0.055 offset
dont: Fading the line in, or scaling it down into a tight mask, which slices the dots and descenders

trigger: reveal a Persian sentence word by word
code: const ws=line.split(' '); ws.forEach((w,i)=>{const pp=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.05,0.32)); if(pp>0) ctx.fillText(w, wordX[i], y-(1-pp)*0.4*size);});
do: Split on spaces only; index 0 is the rightmost word; stagger 40-70ms; travel 0.25-0.5em
dont: Splitting on ZWNJ or per character, which isolates the letters; or letting words fly in from random directions

trigger: curtain wipe a Persian headline from the right
code: const p=PA.ease.outExpo(PA.prog(T,t0,0.7)); ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(0,0,W - p*W, H); ctx.clip(); ctx.fillText(headline, anchorR, y); ctx.restore();
do: Reveal from the right (RTL); feather the edge with a 2-6px gradient or a 1-frame directional blur
dont: Revealing left-to-right in an RTL film, and using a hard 1px clip edge

trigger: feathered wipe where a hard edge looks cheap
code: el.style.maskImage = `linear-gradient(270deg,#000 ${a}%,transparent ${b}%)`; el.style.maskSize='100% 100%';
do: Use a 4-10% transparent band between a and b; 270deg is the RTL-friendly direction
dont: A 1px clip-path edge, which aliases as it travels

trigger: make a Persian headline feel alive without letter-spacing
code: ghost.fillText(s,0,0); ctx.fontVariationSettings = `'wght' ${250+600*p}`; ctx.fillText(s,0,0);
do: Reserve the box with a hidden ghost copy at the final weight (850) so the line cannot reflow; one animated text node per shot
dont: letter-spacing for a spaced look, or slamming wght 100 to 900 instantly, or pumping two nodes at once

trigger: grow one word of a Persian display line
code: const n=Math.round(k*p); ctx.fillText(word.replace(/_+$/,'') + '\u0640'.repeat(n), x, y);
do: Animate an integer count of U+0640 at one or two legal joints plus a small translateX of the surrounding words; hide the steps under a fast easing
dont: Tatweel at a non-joining boundary, or using letter-spacing for the same effect

trigger: type a Persian line on as if being written
code: const shown=s.slice(1,Math.max(1,Math.round(s.length*p))); ctx.direction='rtl'; ctx.fillText(shown+'\u200C', x, y);
do: Append U+200C between the visible prefix and the remainder so the last visible letter keeps its medial form
dont: Rendering the prefix without the ZWNJ, which snaps the final letter to a wrong positional form

trigger: sweep colour across a Persian word without breaking joins
code: for(let i=0;i<g.length;i++){ctx.fillStyle = (W-x[i])/W < p ? accent : ink; ctx.fillText(g[i],x[i],y);}
do: Change only fillStyle per character; spans lay out in logical order so the sweep runs right-to-left for free
dont: Any per-character transform, margin, padding or inline-block, each of which isolates the letter

trigger: rack focus onto a Persian line
code: ctx.filter=`blur(${(1-p)*8}px)`; ctx.fillText(s,x,y); ctx.filter='none';
do: Blur 8px to 0 with opacity following the same p; GPU-cheap and shaping-safe
dont: Blurring twice, or leaving the filter set for the whole frame

trigger: settle a display line into place
code: const v=PA.clamp(PA.ease.spring(p,95,0.42),0,1.25); ctx.translate(0,(1-v)*8); const sy=1-0.10*(1-v); ctx.scale(1.02*sy,sy);
do: Scale a band around 1 (never from zero), keep v >= 0 so the line is visible from frame 0 of the scene
dont: A settle that scales the line from 0, which shows an empty stage at the first reviewable frame

trigger: ground any object
code: const g=ctx.createRadialGradient(x,y0,0,x,y0,r*1.15); g.addColorStop(0,'rgba(0,0,0,0.42)'); g.addColorStop(1,'rgba(0,0,0,0)'); ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(x,y0,r*1.15,r*0.13,0,0,Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
do: Tight to the base, alpha 0.30-0.50, width about 1.15x the object's base width
dont: Leaving an object floating with no ground contact, which is the cheapest visible tell in the batch

trigger: make a flat vector shape read as lit
code: ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(255,236,214,0.85)'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x,y,r,keyStart,keyEnd); ctx.stroke();
do: One bright edge 2-4px toward the key plus the core shadow on the opposite side; that pair is the whole difference between flat and lit
dont: A rim on both sides, which cancels the light direction

trigger: metal cylinder or billet
code: const g=ctx.createLinearGradient(x-w/2,0,x+w/2,0); g.addColorStop(0,'#2b3038'); g.addColorStop(0.45,'#6d7481'); g.addColorStop(0.52,'#c9ced8'); g.addColorStop(0.6,'#7d8492'); g.addColorStop(1,'#23272e'); ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.fillRect(x-w/2,y-h/2,w,h);
do: Two-tone reflection plus an environment line plus a bright edge highlight; scale the treatment with the object so a quarter-size copy is not a quarter-size painting
dont: Reusing one baked 3-stop gradient at 1/4 size on three props

trigger: frosted UI panel or card
code: ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); rr(x,y,w,h,18); ctx.clip(); ctx.filter='blur(10px)'; ctx.drawImage(bg,0,0); ctx.filter='none'; ctx.fillStyle='rgba(255,255,255,0.10)'; ctx.fillRect(x,y,w,h); ctx.restore();
do: Add a 1-2px rim and an inner top shadow 8-14% L* darker; stack cards with a real order
dont: A flat rounded rect with a uniform soft drop shadow, repeated at random angles so the rotated text becomes illegible

trigger: emissive port, lamp or LED
code: const hr=r*PA.clamp(h/320,0.42,1.15); const g=ctx.createRadialGradient(x,y,0,x,y,hr*1.9); g.addColorStop(0,'rgba(255,166,72,0.95)'); g.addColorStop(0.35,'rgba(255,120,40,0.42)'); g.addColorStop(1,'rgba(255,120,40,0)'); ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter'; ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x,y,hr*1.9,0,Math.PI*2); ctx.fill(); ctx.globalCompositeOperation='source-over';
do: Two stops minimum with a hot core and a wide falloff; radius and alpha multiplied by the host's size ratio; one emissive per frame
dont: A fixed-radius glow on every instance, and a flat orange rectangle with no glow at all

trigger: background that must not look like a flat field
code: ctx.fillStyle='#060a12'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); for(let i=0;i<4;i++){const cx=W*(0.5+0.28*noise(i*7.3+0.15*p)), cy=H*(0.4+0.25*noise(i*9.1+0.5)); paint(radial(cx,cy,r,[hue[i],'transparent']));}
do: 3-6 blobs, two hues plus one accent, plus the grain overlay so the gradients never band
dont: A saturated rainbow mesh, or a mesh gradient with no grain, which shows banding on a dark field
cost: ~free (GPU) but a full-screen repaint per frame

trigger: kill gradient banding and add analogue texture
code: ctx.globalCompositeOperation='soft-light'; ctx.globalAlpha=0.05; ctx.drawImage(grainTiles[frame%grainTiles.length], jx, jy, W, H); ctx.globalAlpha=1; ctx.globalCompositeOperation='source-over';
do: Pre-render 6-10 tiles with fixed seeds once, swap the tile by frame index, jitter by 1px; opacity 3-8%
dont: Animating feTurbulence live, and pushing grain past 20%, which reads as screen dirt

trigger: close the frame with corner falloff
code: ctx.globalCompositeOperation='source-over'; const v=ctx.createRadialGradient(W/2,H/2,Math.min(W,H)*0.35,W/2,H/2,Math.max(W,H)*0.72); v.addColorStop(0,'rgba(0,0,0,0)'); v.addColorStop(1,'rgba(8,10,16,0.62)'); ctx.fillStyle=v; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);
do: Corner at least 10% L* below centre; draw it after the type so the whole frame shares the falloff
dont: Even lighting across the frame with no lens

trigger: make CSS colours read as a graded image
code: const aces=x=>{const v=Math.max(0,(x*(2.51*x+0.03))/(x*(2.43*x+0.59)+0.14)); return Math.min(1,v);}; for(let i=0;i<256;i++) lut[i]=aces(i/255);
do: One full-screen pass at the very end, after the type layer, so the type shares the response; exposure 0.9-1.1
dont: Applying the tonemap to the world only, or clipping highlights and calling it a grade
cost: 2-4 ms as one fullscreen pass at 1080x1920 (ESTIMATED)

trigger: three-plane depth in a flat scene
code: layers.forEach((L,i)=>draw(L, camX*(0.15+0.28*i)));
do: 3-6 layers with graduated motion ratios of 0.15-0.35 between neighbours; nearest layer up to 1.25x base drift
dont: One moving layer with everything else static, or all layers translating identically

trigger: sell depth with one shape
code: ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha=0.9; ctx.translate(camX*1.1, 0); roundRect(-W*0.1, H*0.78, W*1.2, H*0.3, 24); ctx.fillStyle=shadow2; ctx.fill(); ctx.restore();
do: A dark or blurred shape crossing a frame edge, moving at the nearest parallax rate; it must cross the edge in both ratios
dont: Foreground that sits entirely inside the frame, which reads as a second subject

trigger: volumetric light shaft
code: [ [1.0,0.14],[2.2,0.07] ].forEach(([k,al])=>{ctx.save(); ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter'; ctx.translate(x,cy); ctx.scale(rx*k/ry,1); const g=ctx.createRadialGradient(0,0,0,0,0,ry); g.addColorStop(0,`rgba(255,214,160,${al})`); g.addColorStop(1,'rgba(255,214,160,0)'); ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(0,0,ry,0,Math.PI*2); ctx.fill(); ctx.restore();});
do: Two nested pools (tight core plus wide penumbra) with no clip path; peak core alpha about 0.14 and never above 0.25
dont: A clipped polygon with a striped fill, where the clip edge shows as a straight decal line

trigger: light pool landing on a floor
code: const g=ctx.createRadialGradient(lx,ly,0,lx,ly,r); g.addColorStop(0,'rgba(255,214,160,0.22)'); g.addColorStop(0.55,'rgba(255,196,140,0.09)'); g.addColorStop(1,'rgba(255,196,140,0)'); ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter'; ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(lx,ly,r,r*0.28,0,0,Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
do: Soft-edged, additive, with falloff and no hard straight edges; it is the thing that replaces s10's hazard-tape decal
dont: A striped orange polygon with straight edges, which reads as tape printed on the deck

trigger: halation on a bright edge
code: ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter'; ctx.globalAlpha=0.18+0.06*Math.sin(t*2); ctx.filter='blur(6px)'; ctx.drawImage(edgeLayer,0,0); ctx.filter='none';
do: A blurred copy of the highlights below threshold, added back; keep it under 25% alpha so it stays light
dont: A hard glow with no threshold, which fogs the whole frame

trigger: dust in a beam
code: for(const m of motes){const x=m.x+8*noise(m.s+t*0.25), y=m.y-14*((t*0.02+m.p)%1); ctx.globalAlpha=0.06+0.14*m.a; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x,y,m.r,0,Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();}
do: 20-40 motes, alpha 0.06-0.20, sizes 2-9px, drawn behind and in front of the subject, positions from PA.rng(seed)
dont: A static dust texture that never moves, or motes drawn only behind the subject

trigger: defocused background field
code: ctx.filter='blur(6px)'; sprites.sort((a,b)=>a.d-b.d).forEach(s=>{ctx.globalAlpha=0.06+0.12*s.a; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(s.x+drift, s.y, s.r*s.d, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();}); ctx.filter='none';
do: At most 30 sprites, alpha 0.06-0.18, size proportional to the depth key, one blur for the whole layer
dont: Hundreds of individually blurred sprites, which eat the frame budget

trigger: canvas2D slice reveal of a still or a rendered layer
code: const s=W/N; for(let i=0;i<N;i++){const p=PA.ease.outQuint(PA.prog(T,t0+d*Math.abs(i-(N-1)/2),0.5)); ctx.drawImage(src, i*s,0, s,H, W-(i+1)*s, (1-p)*sh, s,H);}
do: 6-14 slices with a centre-out eased stagger; keep slice width visually constant across ratios with N = round(N0*W/H)
dont: 60 slices with a linear stagger, which reads as venetian blinds; or one uniform offset for every slice
cost: a few ms at N=12 (2D blit)

trigger: shatter a frame in one WebGL pass
code: float band=floor(uv.y*N); float h=hash21(vec2(band,seed)); float p=smoothstep(0.0,1.0,progress-h*stagger); vec2 q=uv+vec2(dir*(1.0-p)*amp*(0.5+h),0.0); vec3 c=getFromColor(q).rgb*(0.6+0.4*p);
do: Give each slice its own brightness falloff with distance from the frame centre; hash uses the shader's existing seed uniform
dont: All slices moving the same amount with the same brightness, which reads as a solid block
cost: 1 fullscreen pass: ~30-40 ms at 1080p (ESTIMATED from gl-transitions class)

trigger: lens character on a premium or macro shot
code: vec2 d=uv-0.5; float k=0.002*p; float r=getFromColor(uv+d*k).r; float b=getFromColor(uv-d*k).b; gl_FragColor=vec4(r,g,b,1.0);
do: 0.5-2px of radial displacement at the frame edge, applied over the composited frame
dont: Using it at 8px as a style choice, which reads as a broken render
cost: 1 pass, rgb-glitch measured 121 fps at 540x960 MEASURED

trigger: transition between two worlds that share a texture
code: PA.fx.create(cv,{width,height}).transition({from:a,to:b,shader:'noise-dissolve',progress:PA.ease.outCubic(p),seed:7});
do: Both layers rendered by the same pure scene painter; one transition per cut; the window at most 14 frames
dont: Running a shader transition for a second or more, or a CrossZoom sustained shot at about 4fps at 1080p

trigger: hide a cut inside one continuous world
code: PA.fx.create(cv,{width,height}).transition({from:a,to:b,shader:'luma-wipe',progress:p,seed:3});
do: Keep the surviving object continuous across the wipe so the world reads as one place
dont: Cutting between two frames of the same stage with no transition and no change in the world

trigger: open a scene with a small circular reveal
code: PA.fx.create(cv,{width,height}).transition({from:a,to:b,shader:'circle-reveal',progress:PA.ease.outExpo(p)});
do: Anchor the circle on the subject's own position so the reveal implies emphasis
dont: A centred circle reveal on an off-centre subject, which reads as a generic wipe

trigger: whip pan past a cut
code: const s=PA.ease.inOutExpo(p); camX = lerp(x0,x1,s); blurPx = 26*Math.sin(Math.PI*s);
do: 3 frames of travel maximum, directional blur proportional to the camera's own speed at t, hiding exactly one cut
dont: A fast sharp pan with no blur, which reads as a glitch rather than a move

trigger: macro push-in on a detail
code: const cam=PA.camera({keys:[[0,{zoom:1.00}],[2.0,{zoom:1.14}]]}); ctx.setTransform(cam(tLocal)); drawWorld(); ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0); drawType();
do: Build the camera from scene-local seconds since the cut, and reset the transform before the type layer so text is never scaled
dont: Keys in global film time, so the push starts at the film's zero; or a headline scaled by the camera

trigger: pull back to reveal the whole world
code: const cam=PA.camera({keys:[[0,{zoom:1.06}],[1.8,{zoom:0.90}]], ease:PA.ease.inOutSine}); ctx.setTransform(cam(tLocal));
do: Pull-back 1.06 to 0.90 in log space; the subject stays centred and continuous through the move
dont: A linear dollie with no ease, or a cut where a continuous pull-back was available

trigger: a heavy prop lands
code: const v=PA.clamp(PA.ease.spring(p,95,0.42),0,1.25); const x=PA.lerp(x0,x1,v)+antiY; const sy=1-0.10*(1-v); ctx.translate(x,y); ctx.scale(1,sy); drawProp();
do: Anti offset of 6-10px against the entrance direction during the first 90ms, plus a small roll; v stays >= 0 so the prop is visible from frame 0
dont: height*spring(t) as the whole arrival, which makes the prop invisible for about 0.2s and off-frame when it shares the travel parameter

trigger: anticipation before a fast move
code: const anti = p<0.09 ? -6 : 0; const y = PA.lerp(y0,y1,PA.ease.outExpo(PA.prog(p,0.09,0.7))) + anti;
do: 3-8px against the direction for 80-150ms before the move starts
dont: A prop that starts moving with nothing leading it

trigger: follow-through on a trailing element
code: const head=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0,0.45)); const tail=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+0.09,0.45)); drawPaper(PA.lerp(0,1,tail)); drawHand(PA.lerp(0,1,head));
do: Chain 2-4 frames of lag on the trailing element, or use PA.chain(headAt,n,delay,rest) and integrate the table ahead of time
dont: An object that starts and stops rigidly with nothing following it

trigger: a group of items enters
code: list.forEach((it,i)=>{const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.06,0.4)); if(p>0) drawItem(it,p);});
do: 60-90ms between neighbouring items; for Persian text 50ms per line and 40-70ms per word
dont: Every item on the same frame, which reads as one object instead of a list

trigger: a Persian statistic lands
code: const val=Math.round(target*PA.ease.outCubic(p)); ctx.direction='ltr'; ctx.fillText(iso(String(val).replace(/\\d/g,d=>'۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹'[d])), x, y);
do: Isolate only the numeral run with LRI U+2066 and PDI U+2069, set ctx.direction = ltr at the same call, and name the helper iso() so number-lint sees it
dont: Isolating a whole Persian phrase as one LTR run, which reverses the sentence; or letting the count overshoot past the target

trigger: an odometer or split-flap counter
code: digits.forEach((d,i)=>{const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.04,0.5)); ctx.save(); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(cx,cy,cw,ch*1.2); ctx.clip(); ctx.fillText(d, cx, cy+ch*(1-p)); ctx.restore();});
do: One cell per digit sized from the measured widest Persian digit, cell height >= 1.2x so a ۴ is not sliced
dont: A per-letter board or a cell sized for a Latin digit, which slices the Persian glyph

trigger: end card lockup
code: ['mark','headline','deck','cta','legal'].forEach((k,i)=>draw(k, PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.08,0.45))));
do: Own grid and own y ladder; three-step hierarchy; one signal colour; legal row boxes computed before any decoration so nothing crosses them
dont: Letting a hazard band or ribbon run through the ISO row, or letting the headline print across the card's own text

trigger: brand mark in a designed field
code: ctx.beginPath(); hexPath(ctx,cx,cy,r); ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.strokeStyle=accent; ctx.stroke(); drawLogoInside(cx,cy,r*0.62);
do: A stroked hexagon lockup with the mark inside it, on the film's own page field rather than pasted on scenery
dont: A logo pasted flat on a busy background with no field around it

trigger: call to action appears
code: const s=1+0.06*(1-PA.ease.outBack(p)); ctx.save(); ctx.translate(bx,by); ctx.scale(s,s); fillPill(w,h,accent); fillText(cta,inkOnAccent); ctx.restore();
do: Accent pill with the page colour as the label; the accent is reserved for the CTA and the logo only
dont: A flat yellow pill with a low-contrast label, as in the s09 end card

trigger: price or stat stack
code: cards.forEach((c,i)=>{const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.07,0.4)); ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha=p; ctx.translate(c.x, c.y+(1-p)*14); ctx.rotate(c.rot*0.35*p); drawCard(c); ctx.restore();});
do: Settle the rotation with the entrance (rot*p) and keep the rotation under 6 degrees so the Persian price stays legible
dont: Stacking cards at random angles with fully rotated illegible numerals

trigger: a route draws itself on a map
code: const f=PA.ease.inOutSine(p); ctx.setLineDash([len*f, len]); ctx.lineWidth=6; ctx.strokeStyle=route; ctx.stroke(routePath); ctx.setLineDash([]);
do: Draw at constant rate, keep a travelling highlight at the head of the line, and add a soft trail and a small halo
dont: A route line with no head highlight and no trail, which reads as a hairline

trigger: night map atmosphere
code: ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter'; glow(parcel.x,parcel.y, 5+0.6*Math.sin(t*1.5)); labels.forEach(l=>{ctx.globalAlpha=0.35+0.5*p; ctx.fillText(l.t, l.x, l.y);});
do: Bloom around the hero object, street labels at a readable size, bokeh behind, one route line; the only batch frame that reads as cinematography
dont: Flat grey ellipses standing in for searchlights, and a HUD that migrates across the frame

trigger: unify mismatched source imagery
code: ctx.filter='grayscale(1) contrast(1.1)'; ctx.drawImage(src,0,0); ctx.filter='none'; ctx.globalCompositeOperation='multiply'; ctx.fillStyle=shadowHue; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); ctx.globalCompositeOperation='screen'; ctx.fillStyle=highlightHue; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);
do: Two hues only, one for shadows and one for highlights, at restrained saturation
dont: Teal-and-orange at full saturation, which reads as a filter rather than art direction

trigger: both ratios from one film
code: const L=PA.layout(table, ratio); ctx.fillText(headline, L.copyX, L.headlineY);
do: Give the table a full 9x16 and 16x9 entry; re-composition changes the horizon line, the copy rail, the type sizes, the hero band and the end-card grid
dont: Calling layout with one ratio missing, which throws; or changing only the field width and calling it a re-composition

trigger: rhythmic light sweep across the subject
code: const b=PA.beats(bpm)(t); const ang = a0*Math.sin(Math.PI*(b-hit0)/period); ctx.rotate(ang);
do: Drive the beam angle from the beat clock so it crosses the subject exactly on the grid; a zero crossing at the hit, never free rotation
dont: A freely rotating beam, which drifts a few frames off the beat by the end of the shot

trigger: hold a beat with nothing moving
code: if(T>t0+0.3 && T<t1-0.2){ drawAmbientOnly(T); return; } drawEverything(T);
do: 1-2 holds per 15-20s film; let only the ambient layer drift during the hold so the film is never dead
dont: Cutting to a static frame with zero motion, which trips dead-frame detection and kills the rhythm

trigger: hand-drawn stroke appears
code: PA.ink.drawOn(ctx, pts, PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0,0.6)));
do: Use the repo's own drawOn plus seeded wobble, one canvas with many shapes and zero DOM nodes per frame
dont: Per-segment DOM elements, which cost a layout pass per frame

trigger: eyebrow or label above a headline
code: const w=ctx.measureText(label).width; ctx.fillStyle=signal; ctx.fillRect(anchorR-w, y-14, w, 3); ctx.fillText(label, anchorR, y);
do: The rule is right-aligned to the label's own measured width and coloured by signal or accent, never the body colour
dont: A label carried by colour alone at 22px against a 66px headline, which is not enough contrast

trigger: legal or ISO row
code: ctx.globalAlpha=0.55*p; ctx.letterSpacing='0.02em'; ctx.fillText(legal, anchorR, y); ctx.letterSpacing='0px';
do: Tracking is a Latin-only device: 0.02em is allowed on this Latin/digit row and never on a Persian run; alpha about 55%
dont: Applying the same tracking to the Persian copy above it, which severs the joins

trigger: a deck line under a headline
code: const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+0.09,0.4)); ctx.globalAlpha=0.7*p; ctx.fillText(deck, anchorR, headlineY+0.9*size);
do: Deck weight 300-400 at 34-40px and 70% alpha, so hierarchy is carried by weight and colour and not only by size
dont: The deck set as the headline at 40%, the same weight and full opacity

trigger: build the hero-contrast frame
code: const p=PA.ease.outExpo(PA.prog(T,t0,1.0)); drawField(1-0.35*p); drawHero(0.8+0.2*p); drawType(p); applyGrade();
do: One frame per film where type, scale, colour and light all peak together; ideally the end card, and clean enough to screenshot
dont: Two frames claiming the peak, so neither lands

trigger: a product row instead of a copy-paste
code: for(let i=0;i<n;i++){const r=seeded(i); const p=PA.ease.outCubic(PA.prog(T,t0+i*0.07,0.4)); draw(rot:r.rot*p, y:y0+r.dy, scale:0.88+0.12*r.d);}
do: Vary rotation by at least 3 degrees, depth by at least 12% scale, and occlusion order per instance, all from a seeded PRNG
dont: Three identical copies of the hero asset at 1/4 scale on one shadow

trigger: ambient drift so the frame is never dead
